It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be converted into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknotting operations, combined with some variations in the diagram configuration, which are referred to as Reidemeister moves. Unknotting operations hold significant value in the field of knot theory; they serve a purpose in analyzing the intricacy of knots and knot-related properties. Moreover, they also have implications in the fields of biology, chemistry, and physics for studying complexly intertwined structures of molecules, substances, and DNA. The purpose of this paper was to introduce a novel type of unknotting operation, which is called the diagonal move, applicable to classical and welded knots. The study shows that the cross-over change, the delta-move, the sharp-move, the gamma-move, the n-gon move, the pass move, and the 4-move can be achieved by applying a sequence of diagonal moves. The study also delves into defining a distance measure that originates from the diagonal move, as well as examining its characteristics.

rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which can be verified through helioseismic techniques. This discrepancy might be attributed to enhanced rotation-induced mixing effects in the star's outer layers as it becomes more luminous. Additionally, the star's equator potentially rotates approximately 10% to 20% quicker than its poles, an inclination that can be determined by analyzing the rotation's dependence on the stellar latitude. This internal rotation gradient could be a result of the star losing angular momentum via a more prominent stellar wind as it becomes luminous. These findings suggest that angular momentum conservation isn't always the dominant factor within stars as they evolve, and tidal forces aren't always effective at keeping synchronised as a result. This discovery has significant implications for understanding how binary systems with synchronized orbits evolve and may require us to reconsider some of the existing theories in this field.

Although machine learning models have been successful in detecting false information, especially when large amounts of labeled data are available, their effectiveness significantly declines when they are applied to emerging events. This limitation creates a significant obstacle for the current methods in detecting false news on unexpected events. Furthermore, the fact that newly emerging events necessitate building a new model from scratch or retraining the existing one, which is often expensive, time-consuming and impractical in real-world settings. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an end-to-end architecture for the detection of false information on unexpected events, called the RGEV model, which leverages the power of graph neural networks and the attention mechanism. The RGEV model utilizes the relationship between pieces of news and user behavior patterns, and employs a dynamic attention mechanism to highlight the most relevant info and relationships. What's more, to enhance the model's capacity to differentiate between misleading and false information, the RGEV model employs a dynamic attention mechanism over text segments. Experimental results on large-scale real-world datasets from WeChat indicate that the RGEV model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, the research team conducts extensive ablation studies and visualizations, demonstrating the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed approach.

Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy (LITT) treats seizures caused by epilepsy in a specific brain area, the mesial temporal lobe. Evaluating the effectiveness of this treatment requires analyzing changes to the treated brain area after LITT, which can be achieved by accurately defining the treated region through image processing. Although deep learning techniques have shown promise in segmenting the treated region, training them on a specific device's images can be challenging due to their variability. To address this issue, we propose an efficient method called Cross-Modal Supervision for segmenting the treated region without requiring images specifically labeled for the therapy, which works by utilizing images specifically labeled for a similar, but not identical, therapy. By utilizing a therapy called radiofrequency ablation as the reference, our method trains a model to accurately define the treated region after LITT with a high level of precision, achieving 91.4% dice score on a specific brain area, the hippocampus, outperforming other similar methods significantly. Through analyzing changes to the treated brain area after LITT to better treat seizures caused by epilepsy, our model contributes significantly to a similar, but not identical, task of segmenting therapy-treated brain areas. Our findings contribute significantly to the similar task of segmenting brain areas treated through therapy, opening up new possibilities for treating seizures caused by epilepsy through customizing therapy devices specifically designed for a similar, but not identical, therapy called radiofrequency ablation.

Menger developed an interest in the abstract concept of angle function, which he then generalized for use in metric and semi-metric spaces. Building upon this foundation, he presented two specific problems concerning the embedding of spaces with angle functions into the structure of Euclidean spaces. This article aims to enhance the definition of angle function to accommodate spaces with the property of betweenness, which it deems a more fundamental framework. Within this revised framework, the article provides solutions to Menger's initially posed problems.

The successful results illustrate the capability of coupling piezoresistive properties with imaging and physics-based analysis to enhance the capacity of self-sensing composite materials to accurately determine damage configurations.

Our findings indicate that rm3's convergence pattern is exponential, while m2 and rm3 exhibit linear and quadratic convergence patterns, respectively, for the primary eigenvalue. a model from distributed data on a graph is a challenging task, especially when it comes to Federated Learning. A significant obstacle in this process is the substantial communication required between nodes and the server. A common strategy used to address this issue involves each node making several local model updates before sharing the updated model with the server. Although this method reduces communication costs, it introduces statistical disparities among the nodes' data sets, leading to slower model convergence and biases. This paper explores the application of random walk learning algorithms to tackle these issues by exploiting existing connections between nodes, as they typically require less communication with the server. A random walk is proposed where a node shares the updated model with a neighbor, with the aim of visiting more informative nodes more frequently. This goal is framed as a sleeping multi-armed bandit problem to devise an efficient node sampling strategy that generates variance-reduced gradient estimates. A novel adaptive random walk learning algorithm is introduced and proven to converge theoretically. Moreover, our results demonstrate its superior performance compared to other random walk algorithms.

Memory (LSTM) have been highly effective in various sequence analysis tasks. However, their substantial size hampers their real-world application due to memory constraints on devices such as mobile phones and embedded systems. As a result, there is an pressing need to optimize LSTM networks. Although techniques like LSTM-AR and Projections have shown successful results in reducing the size of LSTM models, their limitations often lead to a decline in performance. In this paper, we introduce a novel optimization method called Wide-Residual LSTM (WResLSTM). This new optimization technique combines the proven strategy of Residual Connections with that of Projections, thereby subverting the limitations of both. As a result, the WResLSTM model achieves lower rank and residual dimensions, thereby resulting in a more compact model with enhanced accuracy. Experimental conducted on three standard datasets demonstrated that optimizing a pure LSTM model with the WResReslstm technique yields significant results. Specifically, the optimized models exhibit significantly lower rank and residual dimensions, resulting in a model that is not only smaller but also performs at or beyond the performance of unoptimized models. Specifically, the WResLSTM(E0.5) and WResLSTM(E0.3) configurations achieve rank and residual dimensions of 0.5 and 0.3, respectively, yielding a model that is 49% to 71% smaller while maintaining or even improving accuracy by 0.1% to 10%.

the connection between the Galois group of an iterated polynomial and the symmetric group in fields of characteristic zero. A generalization to fields of positive characteristic was achieved by Juul. Building on these findings, we explore a scenario involving an irreducible polynomial F over the algebraic closure of a finite field k(t) with algebraic and separable coefficients. When a generic monic polynomial Phi is composed with F, resulting in a new polynomial with coefficients (a0, a1,...), we identify the Galois group of the composite polynomial's mth iterate. The structure of this Galois group mirrors the (m-folded) iterated wreath product of the symmetric group S_(nd) for n > 0, where n represents the polynomial's degree. In the case of large finite fields, the application of this discovery aligns with analogous theories, including the polynomial equivalent of the Bateman-Horn conjecture, the Chowla's conjecture regarding autocorrelation, and the Chebotarev density theorem over function fields.

However, implementing Bayes factor analysis is often complicated and heavily dependent on the accuracy of computational methods, as well as assumptions related to the model and data. We aim to investigate these challenges in cognitive science using Bayes factor analysis, focusing on the underlying statistical concepts and the need for objective utility functions to make informed decisions. We explore various issues with Bayes factor estimates, including their tendency to err and the reliability of bridge sampling, especially when analyzing complex scenarios. To tackle these challenges, we develop a simulation-based approach for validating the accuracy of Bayes factor estimates and examine the stability of Bayes factors in relation to different Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) draws. We also investigate the variability of Bayes factor estimates and the effectiveness of utility functions in making informed decisions. To facilitate the assessment of Bayes factor reliability, we outline a step-by-step workflow that researchers can use to evaluate the performance of Bayes factor analysis for their individual studies, including an illustrative example from the cognitive sciences. We anticipate that this research will contribute to the development of a robust methodology for evaluating scientific hypotheses based on Bayes factor analysis, along with reproducible code available online.

in wide-field X-ray monitors employing lobster-eye (LE) optics, we propose a concept called multiplexed lobster-eye (MuLE) optics. This configuration involves dividing an LE mirror into multiple sections and using each one to direct X-rays onto a single shared image sensor.
